channel.basis: D7: REV-C1 receipts split 80% Climate Dividend and 20% transition share; the general fund books a 25% income and payroll tax offset (CX) on carbon fees. Added receipts from the higher price and process coverage follow the same rule unless Espen changes it.

budget.freed_d4b_basis: Governing decisions, Oct 26: resizing CAP-7S from $300B to about $105B leaves about $195B less borrowing inside the D4-B investment envelope

O1.label: D7 as is: every added dollar splits 80/20; the general fund pays CX and any channel shortfall

O2.label: CX recapture: 25% of the added receipts go to the general fund; the dividend keeps 55% of the increment

O3.label: Process fee outside the dividend (like REV-C3): process receipts fund the carbon channel first, any surplus to the general fund

O5.label: Process fee pays the package's net cost: each year process receipts cover the package's remaining general-fund cost (carbon-channel shortfall and general-fund items); the rest follows D7

rows.basis: estimate: roughly 3-6 times the pre-2025 BRIC scale (up to $1B a year); NIBS 2019 finds federal mitigation grants save about $6 per $1
rows.label: Standing pre-disaster mitigation fund (BRIC successor): mandatory, formula floor for every state and tribe plus competitive large projects, with anti-impoundment terms

rows.basis: estimate: 5 points on about $20-30B a year of disaster grants
rows.label: Post-disaster mitigation top-up: Hazard Mitigation Grant Program from 15% to 20% of disaster grants (replaces the $1-per-$1 supplemental set-aside, which would be pro-cyclical and unbounded)

rows.basis: estimate: about 1.1-1.5 million eligible current policies at $600-1,000 average discounts plus 0.3-0.8 million new low-income policies; FEMA's own legislative proposal sets the same eligibility test (FEMA NFIP proposal item 9); Risk Rating 2.0 cut new policies 11-39% (Dec 2025 study cited by senators)
rows.label: NFIP means-tested premium assistance for low- and moderate-income primary residences (at or below 120% of area median income, capped at 400% of poverty, non-transferable), with take-up outreach

rows.basis: scaled: CBO scored the 2007 bill's $17.5B forgiveness at about $1.2B net over ten years because repayment was not expected; face value $22.5B
rows.label: NFIP debt resolution: cancel the $22.5B debt with a multi-year reauthorization (to 2035) and a reserve rule

rows.basis: scaled: the Forest Service projected $50B over ten years in 2022 ($20B on its land, $30B elsewhere); federal increment over FY2025's $7.3B wildfire funding
rows.label: Wildfire risk reduction above the current baseline (Wildfire Crisis Strategy completion, community defensible space, prescribed-fire workforce)
Extreme heat: heat as an eligible hazard, cooling-center and tree-canopy grants, CDC Climate-Ready States and Cities to all 50 states (LIHEAP cooling is in CLI-5)
Universal Survivor Application and estimate-based Public Assistance: program effect of faster, more complete aid (administration is priced in CAP-7)

rows.basis: estimate: about 8-12 million eligible households in high-risk counties at $200-400 average help
rows.label: Climate Insurance and Recovery Affordability Program: premium help for low- and moderate-income owners and renters facing wind, wildfire and hail risk, available from FY2030 without waiting for a reinsurance backstop; states must adopt CLI-8 codes within three years to keep it

rows.basis: estimate: about $250,000 average acquisition (local examples near $214,000) plus about 10% activity costs (Curran-Groome et al. 2022), 75% federal share; Iowa buyouts returned a benefit-cost ratio of 2.19
rows.label: Voluntary buyout and relocation program: 10,000-25,000 properties a year, receiving-community investment, renter relocation aid

rows.basis: estimate. Layer pricing: modeled expected loss in a 1-in-100 to 1-in-250 layer is roughly 0.6-1.0% of limit a year, about $1-1.5B on $150B; premiums at 1.3-1.5x cover it in expectation, and the cost range is pricing error, ramp-up before the fund accrues and draws beyond the recoupment cap. Anchors (sourced): U.S. insured catastrophe losses about $100B in 2025, 12% above the 10-year average (Gallagher Re); the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund carries $17.0B of claims-paying capacity on a $1.29B premium (2025-26) and leans on post-event bonds; TRIA's federal share above a program trigger with mandatory recoupment is the scoring precedent; Sen. Schiff's INSURE Act (July 2025) proposes a Treasury program above a catastrophe threshold
rows.d4: permanent (expected net cost scored): risk-priced premiums at 1.3-1.5x modeled expected loss build a fund; Treasury borrowing authority up to the $150B cap pays claims the fund cannot; a TRIA-style recoupment surcharge on all residential property premiums (flat up to 1%, risk-weighted above; capped at 3% a year, up to 15 years, about $75B) repays it; any unrecouped draw is a disclosed contingent liability in every D4 test
rows.label: Federal residential catastrophe reinsurance facility (Treasury): reinsures insurers' residential wind, wildfire, hail and (opt-in) earthquake losses between a state-level 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 year industry loss, 10% retained by insurers, $150B annual cap; only in states with CLI-8 codes and disclosure (decided Oct 27); flood stays in NFIP
